title: Human basophil degranulation triggered by very dilute antiserum against IgE
central_claims: Serially diluted anti-IgE triggers basophil degranulation beyond molecular presence, depending on shaking; water organization proposed speculatively.

source_manifest.title: Human basophil degranulation triggered by very dilute antiserum against IgE
source_manifest.finding: Original author text; central claims recorded before outcome grading.

source_manifest.title: Human basophil degranulation is not triggered by very dilute antiserum against human IgE
source_manifest.finding: Hirst and colleagues find no dilution-response evidence consistent with the original claim; complete abstract read.

source_manifest.title: Mechanical agitation of very dilute antiserum against IgE has no effect on basophil staining properties
source_manifest.finding: Twenty-four blinded experiments find no effect of vortexed ultradilute anti-IgE on basophil staining.

source_manifest.title: Memory of water revisited
source_manifest.finding: Original authors dispute Hirst’s methods, including blood selection, controls and centrifugation. The same printed page includes independent Wiegant correspondence reaffirming null blinded experiments.

source_manifest.title: Replication study concerning the effects of homeopathic dilutions of histamine on human basophil degranulation in vitro
source_manifest.finding: Discussion distinguishes failed controlled replication of anti-IgE activation from the different histamine-inhibition literature; new histamine effects are control-sensitive.

research.summary: Ultradilute anti-IgE activation failed independent blinded tests. Authors contested procedural changes, while later work distinguishes this failed claim from separate histamine-inhibition experiments. Attention and follow-up are preserved without treating them as confirmation.
